title: Unbounded ringed-site sections agree with underlying abelian sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use sheaves of $B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and K-injective total derived sections [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. For $K\in D(B)$ write $K_{\mathrm{ab}}$ for the image under termwise forgetting of the module structure. For every object $U\in\mathcal C$, the canonical comparison
$$R\Gamma(U,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,K_{\mathrm{ab}})$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. Here sections on either side mean derived evaluation at $U$, equivalently global sections on the localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The comparison is natural in $K$ and in site arrows $V\to U$, with the actual restriction maps. For a module K-injective representative $I$ of $K$ and an abelian K-injective replacement $a:I_{\mathrm{ab}}\to J$, it is represented by $\Gamma(U,a):\Gamma(U,I)\to\Gamma(U,J)$. No assertion that forgetting preserves K-injectivity is made.

source.place: Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded (1),(2), including its comparison via a module K-injective and an abelian K-injective replacement; restriction naturality of the displayed Gamma(U,a) maps.

proof.text: Fix $U$. The slice $\mathcal C/U$ is small: its objects and arrows are subsets of the corresponding sets of objects and arrows with a map to $U$. Write $B_U=B|_U$ and $\mathbf Z_U=\underline{\mathbf Z}$ on this slice. Integer multiples of $1$ give a ring-sheaf map $\mathbf Z_U\to B_U$. Modules over $\mathbf Z_U$ are precisely abelian sheaves: the integer action is forced to be repeated addition, and for a locally represented integer section the action is obtained by gluing these integer actions; additivity makes every abelian sheaf morphism linear. This identification leaves underlying groups, differentials, kernels and sheafified cokernels unchanged, hence also quasi-isomorphisms and K-injectivity. Restriction of scalars along $\mathbf Z_U\to B_U$ is therefore forgetting the $B_U$-action. Restriction to the slice is exact: kernels restrict sectionwise; a section of a cokernel is locally represented by a section of the target, and the same covering families are available in the slice. Thus restriction commutes with cohomology and preserves quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded: identification of abelian sheaves with integer-sheaf modules; elementary localization and scalar-action identifications

proof.text: Choose a module K-injective representative $I$ for $K$ and an abelian K-injective replacement $a:I_{\mathrm{ab}}\to J$. These exist for the small site with ring sheaf $B$, and with ring sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z}$, respectively. For any such choices the localized restriction lemma makes $I|_U$ K-injective over $B_U$ and $J|_U$ K-injective over $\mathbf Z_U$. Step 1 makes $a|_U$ a quasi-isomorphism from the scalar restriction of $I|_U$ to $J|_U$. In particular it is a K-injective replacement of that scalar restriction; K-injectivity of $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ is neither needed nor inferred.

source.place: Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded, first paragraph of proof; Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open

proof.text: Apply the scalar-sections comparison lemma on $\mathcal C/U$ to $R=\mathbf Z_U$, $S=B_U$, $L=I|_U$ and the replacement $a|_U$. Its normalization says that $\Gamma(\mathcal C/U,a|_U)$ is a quasi-isomorphism representing the canonical natural isomorphism from $B_U$-derived sections to integer-sheaf-derived sections after scalar restriction. The localization comparison identifies both endpoints with the derived evaluations at $U$, by the literal identities $(I|_U)(\mathrm{id}_U)=I(U)$ and $(J|_U)(\mathrm{id}_U)=J(U)$. The representing map is consequently exactly $\Gamma(U,a)$. Since a quasi-isomorphism becomes invertible in the derived category, this proves the claimed canonical isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, including its representative formula for every allowed $I,a,J$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, via the existing general scalar-sections comparison; Tag 0D6F, lemma-unbounded-cohomology-of-open; comparison formula of Tag 0D6J

proof.text: Naturality in $K$ follows from naturality in the derived argument of the scalar comparison and both localization isomorphisms. To verify the actual restrictions, use the same $I,a,J$ for every object. For $v:V\to U$, the equality $J(v)\,a_U=a_V\,I_{\mathrm{ab}}(v)$ holds degreewise because $a$ is a morphism of complexes of sheaves. Hence the square of sections complexes with horizontal maps $\Gamma(U,a),\Gamma(V,a)$ and vertical maps the actual restrictions commutes. The localization identifications are sectionwise identities and relocalization is also sectionwise the identity, so this square is exactly the claimed derived restriction square. Its images in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ still commute. The canonical resolution identifications from step 3 make this independent of the choices.
